newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb assembly restores stadium's banned name.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb assembly restores stadium's banned name.

text.p: Zagreb city assembly, controlled by opposition parties, dealt an apparent political blow to Croatian President Franjo Tudjman on Wednesday by changing the name of the capital's main football stadium.
The state news agency HINA said the assembly restored the stadium's old name of Dinamo, which Tudjman abhorred as reminiscent of the old communist era.
Tudjman had provoked a row with Dinamo's die-hard fans, the "Bad Blue Boys", when he changed the name of the stadium's football team from Dinamo to Croatia in keeping with the new nationalist era.
Demands for the return of the name of Dinamo blended into a broader popular movement for more democracy in a country that has suffered from war and wartime authoritarianism.

Tudjman had no immediate reaction to the assembly's decision and it was not clear if the change would stick. Members of the ruling HDZ party, unwilling to give up power in Zagreb despite losing elections there last October, are boycotting assembly meetings.
